Sequences and notation: A sequence is an ordered list of terms, and a_n is the nth term. An explicit formula gives a_n from n, for example a_n = 3n - 1. A recursive formula gives the first term and a rule using the previous term, for example a_n = a_(n-1) + 3. The factorial n! is the product of the whole numbers from n down to 1, so 5! = 120 and 0! = 1. To write a formula, look at how the terms change.
Arithmetic sequences: An arithmetic sequence adds the same common difference d each time, so d = a_(n+1) - a_n. The explicit formula is a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d. Given two terms, divide the difference of the terms by the number of steps to find d. The arithmetic mean of two numbers is their average. To test whether a number is in the sequence, solve for n and check that it is a whole number.
Arithmetic series and sigma notation: A series is the sum of a sequence. The sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic series is S_n = n(a_1 + a_n)/2, which is the number of terms times the average of the first and last term. Sigma notation adds terms for k from a start value to an end value, and a sum from k = a to b has b - a + 1 terms. The sum of k from 1 to n is n(n + 1)/2.
Geometric sequences: A geometric sequence multiplies by the same common ratio r each time, so r = a_(n+1)/a_n. The explicit formula is a_n = a_1 * r^(n - 1). A negative ratio makes the signs alternate. Given two terms, divide them and take a root to find r. The geometric mean of a and b is the square root of ab. Constant differences mean arithmetic; constant ratios mean geometric.
Finite geometric series: The sum of the first n terms of a geometric series with r not 1 is S_n = a_1(1 - r^n)/(1 - r). If r = 1, then S_n = n * a_1. The formula uses r^n, not r^(n-1). To use it, find a_1, r and n first, using the nth term formula if the number of terms is not given. Sigma notation such as the sum of 2^k from k = 1 to 6 can be evaluated with this formula.
Infinite geometric series: An infinite geometric series converges only when |r| < 1, and then its sum is S = a_1/(1 - r). If |r| is 1 or more, the series diverges and has no finite sum. Repeating decimals are infinite geometric series, so 0.777... = 0.7/(1 - 0.1) = 7/9. A bouncing ball problem adds the initial drop to twice the sum of the rebound heights.
